children: Asian currencies are mixed against the greenback. Although the Federal Reserve's decision to hold rates was widely expected, it drew dissents from two officials in favor of a quarter-point increase. Investor attention now turns to the U.S. PCE inflation data due later Thursday for signs that higher energy costs are feeding into underlying price pressures, MUFG Bank's Lloyd Chan says in a report. A firmer print could further reinforce expectations for a December Fed hike and keep Treasury yields elevated, the senior currency analyst adds. The U.S. dollar is little changed at 157.84 yen, but is 0.7% lower at 1,332.00 won, while the Australian dollar is 0.2% higher at US$0.7065, LSEG data show.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)
